polylogue-czh1x.description: Class bead from the s5iyt fix (PR #4028, 2026-08-19): bootstrap._TIER_PROTOTYPES caches one materialized database per (tier, version) and page-copies it into later empty connections; the key deliberately excludes the DDL because ARCHIVE_DDL_BY_TIER is a production constant — but anything that varies the DDL at the same (tier, version) (tests monkeypatching; hypothetically a future dynamic-DDL path) receives a prototype that does not match the DDL it claims to represent. #4028 fixed the test-side symptom (SOURCE-scoped cache clearing around the DDL-patching module); closing the CLASS means a DDL-aware key (hash of the tier DDL string, cheap) — a hot-production-path change deliberately kept out of the test-only PR. Relates to the A1 schema-identity family (workload_artifacts keys on DDL_BY_TIER hash already — same idea one layer down) and to yh20k (embeddings excluded from this same cache).
polylogue-czh1x.notes: 2026-08-21: implemented at 5bc514d48. Tier prototypes now use the rendered DDL digest in both the in-memory key and backing filename, so same-tier same-version DDL variants cannot page-copy or overwrite one another. The regression verifies baseline DDL, a variant-only table, then the restored baseline again; the previous SOURCE-only prototype-clearing fixture is removed as obsolete. Verification: devtools test tests/unit/infra/test_workload_artifacts.py tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tier_init.py tests/unit/devtools/test_verify.py tests/unit/cli/test_archive_maintenance_cli.py tests/unit/storage/test_durable_change_train.py: 494 passed in 189.69s; devtools verify --quick: success in 48.85s.
polylogue-czh1x.title: Tier-prototype cache key excludes the DDL: a poisoned prototype can be page-copied to consumers whose DDL differs

polylogue-kn6nz.description: Found during PR #4009 (A1 cache work): tests/infra/workload_artifacts.py _validate_artifact catches sqlite3.Error broadly and returns None, so a TRANSIENT lock (concurrent xdist reader) is indistinguishable from a corrupt artifact and triggers a spurious full republish (multi-second) — hit twice while building the A1 tests. Undercuts the warm-hit cheapness the validate-once memo buys. Fix needs care distinguishing contention (retry/backoff) from corruption (refuse); out of #4009 scope by design.
polylogue-kn6nz.notes: 2026-08-21: implemented at 5bc514d48. _validate_artifact now treats SQLite OperationalError lock or busy failures as bounded validation contention, retrying for up to five seconds before propagating rather than deleting and republishing the immutable cache artifact. Other SQLite failures remain invalid-artifact paths. Regression tests prove transient contention is distinguished and retried. Verification: devtools test tests/unit/infra/test_workload_artifacts.py tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tier_init.py tests/unit/devtools/test_verify.py tests/unit/cli/test_archive_maintenance_cli.py tests/unit/storage/test_durable_change_train.py: 494 passed in 189.69s; devtools verify --quick: success in 48.85s.
polylogue-kn6nz.title: _validate_artifact treats a transient SQLite lock as corruption and triggers a full artifact republish

polylogue-l218h.description: Found during the 2026-08-19 overnight campaign run. Some lane-init-provisioned worktrees (h1-missing-instruments, h5-quality-sweep, coordinator merge-terminal) compute environment digest polylogue-e962f60d... while the main checkout and earlier lanes (wsb-mechanical-sweep, a1-seeded-cache) compute the digest the recorded graph belongs to. Consequence: lane-init seeds the graph ("lane verifies start warm") but the graph belongs to the OTHER digest, so the lane plain `devtools verify` selects `bootstrap (absent)` and silently runs the FULL corpus (~45 min); three such runs stacked took the host to load 21 and put 2700s runtime caps at risk. One coordinator reproduction also confirmed env-var sensitivity: a clean shell without HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE flips the digest (env vars are declared digest inputs — that part is by design; the lane-vs-main split is not). SUSPECTS to check: installed-distribution-set drift between the main venv and `uv sync --extra dev-common --extra speed` (lane recipe), interpreter identity, tests/conftest hashing across merge-commit heads. FIX SHAPE: (a) make lane-init VERIFY digest equality with the main checkout after provisioning and warn/refuse on mismatch (a seeded-but-unattestable graph is worse than none — it advertises warmth it does not have); (b) either align the lane sync extras with the digest inputs or exclude genuinely-irrelevant distribution differences from the digest; (c) `devtools why` prediction should be surfaced by verify itself before committing to a bootstrap in a worktree (one line: "environment absent — this will execute the full corpus; Ctrl-C now if unintended"). Interim campaign policy (ORCHESTRATION learned facts 2026-08-19): lanes run `devtools why` before any plain verify; coordinator records merge receipts centrally from the main checkout.
polylogue-l218h.notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (lane-a1, 2026-08-19): devtools workspace lane-init does NOT pin the interpreter — uv provisioned a uv-downloaded free-threaded CPython 3.14.5 instead of the main checkout Nix 3.14.4; on that build `import hypothesis` dies in sysconfig (AttributeError installed_base), killing tests/conftest.py, so every devtools test in the lane aborts at collection; the lane then REPROVISIONS against the correct interpreter — and the reprovision after lane-init already seeded the graph is the digest drift. Second defect same area: a lane .cache/testmondata can be 99MB yet an EMPTY database (quick_check ok, zero sqlite_master rows) — seeding produced a valid-but-empty graph. FIX: lane-init passes --python <main-checkout interpreter> to uv (derive from the main venv), verifies the interpreter identity in its guard step, and verifies the seeded graph is non-empty; small devtools PR, dispatching to the lane that diagnosed it.
CORRECTIONS 2026-08-19 (later same night, measured by two independent lanes): (1) STRIKE the empty-graph finding — the 99MB-empty-database observation was the reporting lane probing the WRONG PATH (.cache/testmondata instead of .cache/testmon/testmondata) and reading back its own sqlite3.connect artifact; the real lane graph is healthy (99.8MB, 7 tables, 4 environments). (2) The digest split is NOT lane drift in the original sense: e962f6 is shared by ALL lane-init lanes (same lockfile+extras), while main computes a different digest — because the digest hashes the installed DISTRIBUTION SET and the main devshell venv is synced with a different extras set than lane-init (dev-common+speed). Consequence: seeded graphs can NEVER attest in lanes as provisioned — lanes always bootstrap; main always warm (main receipts all night: "full (valid), native environment is current"). A fresh lane also measured a THIRD digest post-pinning, consistent with 08-18 digest-input commits (#3987 dep bump + #3990/#3993/#3994/#4000) churning values — some cross-claims between lanes about main-not-matching-its-own-graph remain unreconciled; trust receipts over ad hoc probes. (3) Interpreter half CONFIRMED and fixed in PR #4017 (pin via sys._base_executable, post-sync identity guard, honest warm/cold seed reporting keyed on digest CONTAINMENT). (4) REMAINING FIX for genuinely-warm lanes: align lane-init sync extras with the main devshell extras set (or exclude irrelevant distributions from the digest) — until then, the campaign policy (lanes gate on focused+quick; coordinator records receipts on main) stands. (5) Dispatch-env hazard, same family: harness-spawned lanes inherit the devshell _PYTHON_SYSCONFIGDATA_NAME/PYTHONPATH/PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX, which kills pytest in a lane venv until scrubbed, and pr-scope/gh need SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt — scrub landing as a #4017 rider.
polylogue-l218h.title: Lane venvs compute a divergent testmon environment digest: seeded graphs never attest, lane gates silently bootstrap

polylogue-oizgt.acceptance_criteria: 1. A fresh lane and the authoritative checkout compute the same environment digest under the campaign's declared environment. 2. A seeded lane graph validates as warm without a full-corpus bootstrap when its source graph is valid. 3. A changed semantic dependency or conftest invalidates the digest and remains cold. 4. Focused lane-init/testmon lifecycle tests and devtools verify --quick pass with receipts.
polylogue-oizgt.description: Align lane-init lane provisioning with the coordinator's authoritative testmon environment distribution set so seeded graphs attest as warm when the code and test inputs are otherwise identical. Preserve explicit digest inputs that affect test semantics; document any intentionally excluded distributions.
polylogue-oizgt.design: Measure the main checkout and a freshly provisioned lane under identical declared HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE/POLYLOGUE_CI inputs. Compare interpreter, installed distribution set, conftest/devtools digest inputs, and native graph attestation. Update the lane provisioning recipe or digest contract using the existing devtools substrate; do not make invalid or incomplete graphs warm by weakening validation.
polylogue-oizgt.title: Align lane sync extras with the main testmon environment
